messages:
alex: quick heads up — several dedicated GPU hosts in eu-west-1 failing container image pulls since ~10:20 UTC. CI and k8s show image pull backoff. logs have TLS handshake and i/o timeout intermittently :(
maria-network: which VPC/subnet? do we have an interface endpoint for ECR in that VPC?
alex: vpc-0a1b2c, private subnets ml-a/ml-b. we do have a vpce for ECR (vpce-0f1e2d). docker daemon logs show a mix of 'i/o timeout' and 'tls: handshake failure'. curious thing: curl to the api.ecr private IP sometimes connects, sometimes hangs.
ken: can you paste nslookup + describe-network-interfaces for the vpce ENIs? also tcpdump if possible.
alex: dropping outputs below — small redacted snippets.

```
$ nslookup api.ecr.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com
Server: 169.254.169.253
Address: 169.254.169.253#53

Name: api.ecr.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com
Address: 10.0.58.73

$ aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0a1b2c Name=attachment.instance-owner-id,Values=vpce
---
NetworkInterfaces:
 - NetworkInterfaceId: eni-0aa11bb22
   SubnetId: subnet-ml-a
   PrivateIpAddress: 10.0.58.73
   Groups: [ sg-vpce-ecr ]
 - NetworkInterfaceId: eni-0cc33dd44
   SubnetId: subnet-ml-b
   PrivateIpAddress: 10.0.59.12
   Groups: [ sg-vpce-ecr ]

$ aws ec2 describe-network-acls --network-acl-ids nacl-0abcde
Entries:
 - RuleNumber: 100
   Protocol: 6
   RuleAction: deny
   Egress: true
   PortRange: {From: 1024, To: 65535}
 - RuleNumber: 110
   Protocol: 6
   RuleAction: allow
   Egress: true
   PortRange: {From: 443, To: 443}
```

maria-network: aha — that NACL looks suspicious. we allow 443 outbound but actively deny ephemeral ports egress. interface endpoints are stateful at the ENI level but NACLs are stateless — replies from the endpoint will be using high ports. if egress ephemeral is denied, instance -> vpce SYN may go out but SYN-ACK gets dropped on return, causing TLS handshake failures / timeouts.

rachel-sre: confirmed with tcpdump on one node — we see SYN to 10.0.58.73:443, but no SYN-ACK. when we temporarily remove the deny rule, SYN-ACK appears and handshake completes.

ken: quick mitigation: add an explicit allow rule for ephemeral 1024-65535 egress on that NACL (or remove the deny). long term: we should audit NACLs on subnets hosting interface endpoint ENIs and add a rule to our network hardening checklist.

alex: applied allow for 1024-65535 egress on nacl-0abcde at 10:58 UTC, re-triggered a couple of image pulls — they all succeeded. marking this as fixed for now.

deploy-bot: deploy #deploy/dedicated-gpu-pool-2026-03-18 succeeded (post-fix smoke)

maria-network: root cause = legacy restrictive NACL that blocked ephemeral egress to PrivateLink ENIs. note: many teams lock down NACLs aggressively; PrivateLink requires allowing ephemeral return ports (or else you get asymmetric drop).

rachel-sre: action items:
 - add NACL check to infra-guard (coverage for any subnet with interface endpoints)
 - doc note in runbook: "PrivateLink endpoints require ephemeral return port allowances" with example NACL rules
 - follow-up: alert when interface endpoint health checks show >10% connection failures for >5m

alex: adding runbook PR now. thanks all :thumbsup!

ken: optional: consider using security groups + route tables to reduce reliance on NACLs for this VPC, or move vpce ENIs into subnets with permissive NACLs if we must keep strict per-subnet lists.

rachel-sre: will own the runbook + create an automated scan to find NACLs that deny 1024-65535 egress in any subnet that contains /= VPCE ENIs.

alex: closing thread — fixed in prod and added follow-ups.
